content.title: About
content.content: The Burrito Bowl with chicken and beans is a Mexican‑inspired dish that combines rice, grilled chicken pieces, black or red beans, fresh vegetables, salsa and sour cream in a single bowl. It offers a balanced mix of protein, complex carbs and fiber for a satisfying meal.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The burrito bowl gained popularity in the United States in the early 2000s as a lighter alternative to the traditional wrapped burrito.
Chicken is usually seasoned with chipotle or other smoky spices, giving the bowl a distinctive flavor.
Beans provide a plant‑based source of protein and iron, and are often used in vegetarian versions of the bowl.
Traditional bowls use corn rice, but brown rice or quinoa can be substituted for added nutrition.
The dish is easily customized for dietary needs, such as swapping sour cream for guacamole or cheese for a vegan alternative.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Chicken supplies high‑quality animal protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Good source of fiber
items.content: Beans and vegetables add soluble and insoluble fiber, supporting digestive health.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Chicken and beans are rich in vitamin B6 and folate, which play key roles in energy metabolism.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with traditional beef‑filled burritos, this bowl contains less saturated fat, benefiting heart health.

items.title: Antioxidants from veggies
items.content: Fresh tomatoes, peppers and salsa provide lycopene and vitamin C, protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to chicken, experiencing skin reactions or digestive issues.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Salsa, sauces, and canned beans can be high in salt; people with hypertension should monitor portions.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: Adding generous amounts of cheese, sour cream, or guacamole can make the bowl calorie‑rich.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Chicken must be cooked thoroughly to avoid the risk of salmonella.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the bowl in a deep plate or bowl. Mix the ingredients together, then drizzle your favorite sauce. It can be eaten with a fork or spoon, and topped with lime, guacamole, or crunchy tortilla chips for extra texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Prepared bowl can be kept in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Store chicken and beans separate from fresh veggies to maintain crunch. When reheating, add a splash of water or sauce to prevent drying out.
